name: Homaranismo
summary: Homaranismo (Humanitism) is L. L. Zamenhof's ethical and quasi-religious philosophy of human fraternity, built on the golden rule and meant to give people of every religion and nationality a neutral common ground. It holds that all peoples are equal, that a country belongs equally to all its inhabitants, and that ethnic nationalism is group egoism to be outgrown, while each person keeps their own language, faith and family customs. It seeks gradual, unforced convergence, with a neutral language (Esperanto) in cross-group dealings, and says nothing about economic policy.
scope: The doctrine as Zamenhof set it out: the 1901 Russian 'Hillelism' (Dogmas of Hillelism) and the later Homaranismo declaration (1906 anonymous, 1913 under his name), as described by Wikipedia and Zamenhof's biography. Because it is an ethical-religious philosophy with no economic or institutional programme, most answers on economics and institutions are low-confidence inferences from its humanist principles. Excludes later Esperanto-movement politics (such as the Raumists or Esperanto's secular neutrality) and Baha'i interpretations by Lidia Zamenhof.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Zamenhof's texts never address health policy; fraternity and justice for all people suggest support for guaranteed care, but this is an inference.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: No wage policy is stated; the ideal of equal and absolute justice leans toward fairer pay, an inference only.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The doctrine is silent on economic organisation and adherents have held both market and interventionist views.

public-ownership.rationale: Nothing in Hillelism or Homaranismo speaks to ownership of industry; adherents are not committed either way.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Not discussed; a justice-and-fraternity ethic suggests mild sympathy for redistribution, inferred.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are not mentioned; solidarity across groups fits the ethic, so a weak inference of support.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property rights are never discussed in the sources; no stated position.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The doctrine has no economic content, so adherents are split or indifferent.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; the ethic of treating others as one wishes to be treated points away from cutting aid, inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: Workplace ownership lies outside the doctrine's concerns.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; the emphasis on equal justice and protecting minorities from majorities suggests wariness of state power, inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Drug policy is outside the sources; personal conscience is stressed but no drug stance follows.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Dogma 2 calls persecuting people for birth into another race, language or religion barbarism, which supports restricting group-hatred, though no law is demanded.

strong-leader.rationale: Not addressed; the demand for equal rights and justice for all citizens implies constraints on rulers, inferred.

state-harmful.rationale: Hillelism envisions states containing equal citizens and speaks of countries with equal rights, so it assumes a state rather than abolishing it.

limit-guns.rationale: Gun policy is never touched; no position can be inferred reliably.

empower-police-military.rationale: The stress on ending violence and its causes suggests reluctance to boost force, inferred.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed by the sources and adherents would differ.

decide-locally.rationale: Dogma 7 wants equal rights in each state; the sources do not discuss levels of government.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not stated; the ethic of fraternity and justice leans toward rehabilitation, inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: Dogma 4 leaves family life to each person's own language and faith, so no view on family structure is imposed.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Zamenhof's writings from 1901-1913 do not address it; modern adherents who follow conscience and equality might support it but it is not documented.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no basis for a position.

more-religion-public.rationale: Dogma 6 wants public institutions to use neutral language and neutral or state festivals, so a larger public role for any one religion is opposed.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Dogma 7 calls for equal and absolute justice but does not mention remedial programmes; support is inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The sources never discuss gender theory.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Dogma 1 calls ethno-national goals group egoism that should fade, and Dogma 9 denies that national languages exist in any real sense.

gradual-change.rationale: The Essence stresses a gradual, unforced merging toward a human-neutral population, and Zamenhof describes no revolutionary programme.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not directly addressed; opposition to ethnic exclusivity and the belief that a country belongs to all inhabitants suggest disagreement, inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Zamenhof hoped a neutral language and understanding would build world peace, but no international institutions are described, so support is inferred.

nation-first.rationale: Zamenhof wrote in 1914 that all nationalism brings humanity great unhappiness, and Dogma 6 says serving only one group's interests is not patriotism.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Dogma 7 treats all violence as violence even when the majority commits it, but intervention is never discussed.

open-borders.rationale: Not stated as policy; the aim of merging into one human-neutral people points toward eventually open borders, inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: Environmental economics is outside the sources.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The sources predate the issue and give no basis for a position.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No stance on technology; Zamenhof's faith in a constructed language is not a general technological optimism.

revolution-justified.rationale: Dogma 7 says violence by any group remains violence, suggesting reluctance to justify revolution, inferred.

experts-over-public.rationale: The sources say nothing on who should decide policy, so adherents have no common view.

central-planning.rationale: The doctrine has no economic programme.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance taxation is a fiscal detail the doctrine never touches.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; adherents would not share a position.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Industrial policy lies outside a doctrine about ethics, language and religion.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The distribution of property is not a subject in Zamenhof's texts.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Nothing suggests abolishing money; the doctrine is a reformist ethic that leaves economic arrangements untouched, an inference.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary institutions are never discussed in Hillelism or Homaranismo.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised class bodies are not mentioned, and the doctrine is about ethnic and religious equality, not labour organisation.

one-party-rule.rationale: Dogma 7 demands equal rights for all citizens and Dogma 3 a state belonging to all inhabitants, which is incompatible with guided single-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The sources say nothing about forms of government.

democracy-best.rationale: Equal rights for all inhabitants implies sympathy with democratic equality, though Zamenhof never endorses a form of government.

direct-votes.rationale: Zamenhof wrote about equal rights, not the mechanics of lawmaking such as referendums.

workers-councils.rationale: Council power is a socialist idea the sources do not engage with.

right-to-secede.rationale: Dogma 5 bars treating a region of the homeland as one's own on ethnic grounds, which cuts against ethnic secession, inferred.

natural-rulers.rationale: Dogma 2 holds all peoples equal and says people are judged by personal value and deeds, not origin.

political-violence-never.rationale: Dogma 7 calls violence by a group violence even when the majority commits it, yet no pacifist absolute is stated.

war-builds-character.rationale: Dogma 7 says equal rights will abolish the causes of all wars, so war is treated as an evil to remove.

separate-church-state.rationale: Dogma 6 calls for neutral language and neutral or state festivals in public institutions and Dogma 4 for neutral religious principles in dealings across groups.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Dogma 10 treats religious elements other than the golden rule and conscience as myths or customs that should give way to common human-neutral ones.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The sources assume a state of equal citizens and say nothing about privatising justice or defence.

military-superiority.rationale: Not directly stated; the aim of abolishing wars' causes implies rejecting arms rivalry, inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Dogma 3 states a country belongs equally to all inhabitants whatever their language or religion, and that tying national interests to one race is a relic of the rule of the fist and sword.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Hillelism sees conflict as national and religious injustice, not class, and seeks reconciliation; inferred since class is not discussed.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Dogma 7 demands equal justice and rights but not equal economic outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; Dogma 3 favours equal rights for all inhabitants rather than group authority.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Reparations are not addressed, though the doctrine condemns domination of peoples.

civilizational-union.rationale: Dogma 1 rejects group egoism along ethnic lines, and Hillelism wants merging across religions, not unions of co-religionists.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The core law of acting toward others as one wishes to be treated places other-regarding duty above pure self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The ethic stresses duties of fraternity, but equal rights are equally central; no ordering is stated.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy is absent from the early-twentieth-century texts.

limit-population.rationale: Population policy is never raised in the sources.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not addressed; a humanist hope in progress through understanding suggests disagreement, inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The sources have no view on the pace of technological change.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bodily enhancement is an anachronistic question the texts cannot answer.

algorithmic-government.rationale: AI in government is anachronistic for texts of 1901-1913.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Digital privacy is anachronistic and not covered.

restore-past-order.rationale: Dogma 3 calls ethnic claims a leftover from an earlier age of force, and the movement looks forward to a human-neutral society.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Whether policy should follow ideology or outcomes is not a topic in the sources.

direct-action.rationale: Hillelists are told to stay out of language and religion battles; the method is gradual education, so direct action is unlikely, inferred.

means-match-ends.rationale: Dogma 7 treats violence as violence whoever commits it, and the doctrine aims at justice reached by just means.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The doctrine envisions an advanced human community with a common neutral language, the opposite of primitivism.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not addressed; no sign of any such radical economic aim, inferred.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Principles of distribution are not discussed.

production-for-use.rationale: Economic production is not covered by the doctrine.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxian claims about profit are absent from the texts.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rule by one class over others conflicts with Dogma 3 and Dogma 7, which demand equal rights for every group within the state.

collective-farming.rationale: Agrarian organisation is outside the sources.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Zamenhof traces war to national and religious hatred and injustice, not to capitalism, but never discusses capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Not addressed; a communal ethic makes the claim unlikely, inferred.

harm-principle.rationale: The sources set no general limit on state power beyond equal rights.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Dogma 4 and 6 let each group run its own schools and keep its language and faith, so group-linked cultural rights are accepted alongside individual equality.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed; the aim of abolishing war's causes suggests opposition, inferred.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Emigration versus voting as checks on government is not discussed.

state-as-business.rationale: The sources do not compare the state to a firm.

media-academia-power.rationale: Claims about media and universities are not made in the sources.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Dogma 2 holds peoples equal and judges individuals by personal value and deeds, not birth.

organic-representation.rationale: Corporate or family-based representation is not discussed.

total-state.rationale: Hillelists leave family language and religion free (Dogma 4) and oppose imposing one's language or faith on others as barbarism.

national-rebirth.rationale: Dogma 1 calls ethnic national aims group egoism that should vanish and Zamenhof's 1914 letter called nationalism a source of unhappiness.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Dogma 5 forbids calling a foreign state or part of one's homeland one's own on ethnic grounds, and equal rights are meant to end the causes of war.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority resting on personal oaths conflicts with a state of equal citizens under equal justice (Dogma 7).

bound-labor.rationale: Binding people to land and lord contradicts the equality and justice of Dogma 2 and Dogma 7.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The project of a human-neutral language and shared ethic assumes neutral common ground exists, an inference.

universal-morality.rationale: The golden rule is the fundamental law (Dogma 10) and Homaranismo is meant as shared moral principles across religious divisions.

single-common-good.rationale: Dogma 6 defines patriotism as serving the good of all citizens irrespective of group, a common good, though not through a rationalist theory.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Zamenhof left Zionism, arguing in Hillelism that it would fail for lack of a common language, and opposed ethnic nationalism generally.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed; Dogma 5 says the fatherland is where one is born or lives, which opposes ethnic homeland claims, inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: Dogma 9 denies that national languages exist in any real sense and Dogma 6 wants a neutral language in public institutions.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Corporate governance is not a topic of the doctrine.

school-vouchers.rationale: Dogma 6 allows each group its own schools, but funding mechanisms are not discussed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Macroeconomic policy is outside the sources.

economic-freedom.rationale: The link between political and economic freedom is not discussed.

rule-by-example.rationale: The sources do not address rulers' moral example, though they stress ethics.

national-self-determination.rationale: Zamenhof said all nationalism, of the strong and of the weak, brings unhappiness, and favoured equal rights within existing states over ethnic states.

force-without-un.rationale: Not addressed; the aim of ending causes of war suggests reluctance to use force, inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Dogma 10 keeps God, conscience and religious sentiment central, so reason is not the sole guide.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not stated; the equal rights of all inhabitants regardless of origin suggest opposition, inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Not stated for classes, but the doctrine seeks reconciliation among rival groups, inferred.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not addressed; Dogma 4 respects inherited family language and faith, so sacrificing heritage is unlikely.

dominated-front.rationale: Blocs of nations against one another conflict with the aim of dissolving group egoism, inferred.

workers-nation.rationale: Not addressed; both national and class division are alien to its aim of a human-neutral community, inferred.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not addressed; equality of persons by deed and value suggests disagreement, inferred.

ban-interest.rationale: Zamenhof's texts do not discuss lending or usury.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Dogma 2 calls persecution for birth into another race barbarism and Dogma 3 requires equal rights for all inhabitants.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Not addressed; Dogma 3 sees the state as belonging to all its inhabitants, inferred.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is anachronistic and absent from the sources.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Dogma 4 treats forcing one's language or religion on others as barbarism, and Dogma 6 wants equal treatment of all groups.

elite-replacement.rationale: The doctrine rejects hostile conspiracy thinking about ethnic groups, and Dogma 1 calls group hatred something to eliminate.

national-mission.rationale: Dogma 6 rejects serving one group's interests as patriotism and Zamenhof condemned nationalism of the strong as ignoble.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Feminist structural theory is not part of the sources.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The texts contain no populist critique of elites.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Judging people by personal value and deeds (Dogma 2) and equal and absolute justice (Dogma 7) rule out coercive eugenics.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not stated directly, but Dogma 7 demands equal justice independent of strength, inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The proper scope of state functions is not discussed.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The stated aim of gradually merging into one human-neutral population and equality of races (Dogma 2) contradict it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Dogma 2 states that all peoples are equal and individuals are judged by personal value and deeds, and Dogma 7 requires equal and absolute justice.

socialism-one-country.rationale: This is an internal Marxist debate the sources do not touch.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The question is not addressed, though it involves the ethnic-homeland issues Zamenhof rejected.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Dogma 3 asks for equal rights for all inhabitants regardless of religion, which favours a common civil law, though personal-law questions are not discussed.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Dogma 4 condemns forcing religion on others, and one cannot commend or condemn anyone for traditional religion, so legal restriction of conversion is alien.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Animal slaughter law is not covered.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Dogma 6 wants public institutions to be neutral while allowing groups their own schools, so state schools should not teach one religion; inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is opposed to hostile blocs generally, inferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Not directly stated, but the state as belonging to all its inhabitants with equal rights suggests it, inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Dogma 3 says a country belongs to all inhabitants with equal rights and Dogma 7 treats any group violence as violence, even when the majority commits it.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Dogma 7 treats violence against others as wrong whoever commits it, though a total principle is not stated.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Dogma 7 and the Essence see fraternity and equal justice, not struggle between peoples, as the path to human happiness.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Militant-democracy measures are not discussed in the sources.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Equal and absolute justice independent of strength (Dogma 7) fits the idea, though the concept is not used, inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: Not addressed; reliance on gradual moral persuasion points away from it, inferred.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Not stated; fraternity and justice suggest sympathy, inferred.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: British housing policy is far from the sources.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Hillelism rests on the view that peoples of different language and religion can live as equal citizens, and that conflict comes from injustice not diversity.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Equal and absolute justice independent of time and strength (Dogma 7) implies protections should not be suspended, inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: Imposing one view on all conflicts with the stress on equal rights and with the condemnation of forcing language or religion on others.

party-commands-army.rationale: Not addressed; opposition to single-party rule suggests disagreement, inferred.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Not addressed; equal rights for all inhabitants suggest disagreement, inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay for officials is not addressed.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party organisation is not a topic of the doctrine.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Zamenhof saw nationalism as a source of unhappiness and hoped for human unity, but no supranational union is described, inferred.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is not addressed; Hillelism concerns cross-religious ethics.

clerical-rule.rationale: Dogma 10 treats most religious elements as customs and public life as neutral among religions, so clerical rule is opposed.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not addressed; war is rejected but Hillelists are told to stay out of battles between groups, inferred.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not addressed; the stress on freedom of language and faith suggests disagreement, inferred.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliance policy is not addressed, though the doctrine seeks peace.

people-in-arms.rationale: Not addressed; the aim of ending violence suggests disagreement, inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The sources do not compare rural and urban life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Dogma 5 rejects claims to territory on ethnic grounds, which weighs against reunification of a divided nation as a goal.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Populist views of graduates are absent from the texts.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Dogma 2 treats all peoples as equal and Dogma 4 respects each person's own language and faith, though the movement also wants customs to converge gradually.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed; the ethic of the golden rule suggests disagreement, inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Sex education is not discussed in the sources.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Neutral public institutions (Dogma 6) suggest no teaching of one religious doctrine, inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Dogma 5 defines the fatherland as the state where one is born or lives, opposing descent-based ethnic claims.

minority-language-support.rationale: Dogma 7 calls for equal rights for all languages and Dogma 6 for each group to run its own schools.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Equal rights for all religions are stressed, but exemptions from general law are not discussed.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill-style views on conformity are not discussed; Dogma 4 leaves private customs free but states no wider view.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anti-colonial economic theory is not in the sources.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Not addressed; equal rights and justice independent of time and strength suggest disagreement, inferred.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Not stated; universal fraternity and justice suggest support, inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Not addressed; aims of peace suggest disagreement, inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Dogma 5 rejects claiming territory on ethnic or historical grounds, and equal rights are meant to end the causes of conflict.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property theory is not addressed in the sources.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The Soviet Union postdates the texts and is not discussed.

collective-defense.rationale: Treaty alliances such as NATO are not discussed.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Not stated; opposition to forcible group dominance (Dogma 7) suggests agreement, inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Not addressed; neutral public institutions do not imply curbing religious property.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Ceremonial heads of state are not discussed.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Not addressed; opposition to violence suggests disagreement, inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Special autonomy arrangements are not covered.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Dogma 10 treats mythical religious elements as customs to fade and Dogma 2 holds all people equal by deeds.

character-from-environment.rationale: Not addressed; Dogma 2 judges people by deeds but takes no side on nature versus nurture.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Dogma 7 requires equal and absolute justice independent of strength, which leaves no place for a ruler above the law.

space-expansion.rationale: Space is anachronistic and not covered.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is not engaged by the sources.

leader-cult.rationale: The doctrine opposes ethnic or national glorification (Dogma 1, 6) and holds all people equal by personal value.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist-style question the sources never touch.

refugee-return.rationale: Not stated; equal rights and opposition to expulsion by majorities (Dogma 7) suggest support, inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Dogma 5 says one may not call a foreign state or part of one's own homeland mine on ethnic grounds, which rejects such claims directly.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Dogma 4 condemns forcing religion on others and Dogma 10 treats religion as inherited and a matter of conscience.

women-must-cover.rationale: Imposed dress codes conflict with the condemnation of forcing faith on others and with freedom of conscience.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is not discussed, though Zamenhof favoured a common language.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Dogma 1 rejects ethnic group goals and Dogma 5 rejects ethnic claims on territory, which weighs against unions of kin peoples.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Dogma 6 lets each group run its own schools, and Dogma 4 allows each group its own language and faith in family and group life.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Zamenhof left Zionism and held that equal rights for all in their country of residence is the path (Dogma 7), against founding an ethnic homeland.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Zamenhof saw ideas and moral change as central, but the question is not addressed, inferred.

no-bailouts.rationale: Financial rescue policy is not covered.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Dogma 7 warns that majority-dominated states persecute defenders of equal rights and that majority violence is still violence.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Not addressed; a unity-minded outlook suggests disagreement, inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Incentive systems for work are not discussed, though the doctrine is ethical.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Not addressed; violence is condemned in Dogma 7, inferred.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Dogma 2 says people are judged by personal value and deeds, not origin, which opposes inherited privilege.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Dogma 2 holds all peoples equal and Dogma 4 condemns forcing one's language or religion on others.

patriotic-education.rationale: Dogma 6 defines patriotism as serving all citizens, not pride in one group, and wants public institutions neutral; inferred for flag and anthem teaching.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed; equality of all peoples is stated but not the means.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Theories of capitalist crisis are not addressed.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not addressed; opposition to group dominance suggests disagreement, inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This Leninist thesis is not addressed.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Dogma 2 calls persecution for race, language or religion barbarism, which sits badly with a right to discriminate on any grounds.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Equal rights for all languages and religions (Dogma 7) fits entrenched protection against majorities, inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial treaties are not covered in the sources.

elective-rulers.rationale: Not stated; equal citizens suggest rulers chosen by them, inferred.

minority-veto.rationale: Not addressed; protecting minorities does not imply individual vetoes, inferred.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Dogma 7 says defenders of equal rights will be persecuted and not be shaken, but violence is condemned, so resistance is not endorsed.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliament versus monarch is not discussed.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is not addressed in the sources.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The golden-rule ethic implies duties toward others, though class duty is not discussed, inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Hillelists are told to stay out of language and religion battles but to work for equal rights, so full withdrawal is not their stance.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Critical theory of culture is not engaged.

native-born-offices.rationale: Dogma 3 and 5 define citizens by residence and equal rights for all inhabitants, not origin.

party-own-road.rationale: Communist party relations are not addressed.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Dogma 5 rejects ethnic or historical claims over territory and Dogma 7 aims to end causes of wars.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Dogma 3 gives equal rights to all inhabitants, so group leadership claims are inferred to be opposed.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; opposition to ethnic hatred (Dogma 1, 2) suggests support, inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The comparison is not addressed, though the doctrine opposes persecution of groups.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: American history is not covered by the sources.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Gender policy debates are not covered.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence policy is not covered.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Not addressed; Dogma 2 treats peoples as equal but no view on institutions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Not addressed; opposition to force in public life suggests disagreement, inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Not addressed; family life is left to each person's tradition (Dogma 4).

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Corporate takeover policy is not covered.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land tenure systems are not discussed.

single-official-language.rationale: Dogma 6 wants public institutions to use a neutral language but Dogma 7 gives equal rights to all languages and Dogma 4 forbids forcing language on others.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; Dogma 5 rejects ethnic claims on land, which suggests disagreement, inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The legal test for discrimination is not addressed, though the doctrine opposes persecution by origin.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Dogma 7 calls any violence by one group against another violence and the aim is to end the causes of wars.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The doctrine rejects domination of one group over another and seeks to end the causes of wars.

corporate-influence.rationale: Lobbying and campaign finance are not addressed.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local property restrictions are not discussed.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not addressed, though Zamenhof sought peace by other means.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The sources assume laws of equal justice but do not discuss obedience.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Dogma 1 and 2 reject hatred of groups and persecution for birth, and the doctrine was framed against antisemitic propaganda (Wikipedia).

local-production.rationale: Localism in trade is not addressed.

informal-organisation.rationale: Not addressed; the movement used temples and circles, not informal cells.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Not addressed; opposition to nationalism suggests disagreement, inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: Dogma 3 says a country belongs to all inhabitants whatever their religion, and Dogma 4 condemns forcing religion on others.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The doctrine insists on equality among peoples (Dogma 2) and rejects dominance of the strong (Dogma 7).

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The doctrine has no property theory.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Health or welfare delivery is not addressed.

religion-illusion.rationale: Dogma 10 treats God as the highest Power and religion as a matter of conscience, with the golden rule as its core.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Historical judgment on capitalism is not given.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Dogma 9 denies national languages exist as such and Hillelism sought a neutral mixed language, not linguistic purity.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with indigenous nations are not addressed.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Intentional communities are not part of the doctrine.

majority-settlement.rationale: Dogma 3 and 5 reject ethnic claims on regions, and Dogma 7 rejects majority domination of minorities.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine has no economic programme.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Dogma 5 forbids calling territory mine on ethnic grounds and Zamenhof left Zionism, which rests on such a claim.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The doctrine opposes hatred of groups, and Zamenhof's children were murdered in the Holocaust (Wikipedia), though the event postdates his writings.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed; equal rights and the golden rule suggest disagreement, inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Dogma 7 demands equal rights and justice, and violence against dissent is violence.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Dogma 4 condemns forcing religion on others and Dogma 10 holds one cannot commend or condemn anyone for their religion.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Dogma 2 treats all peoples as equal, and domination for the benefit of one group is condemned as injustice.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; religious war is contrary to the aim of ending conflict, inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Religious litmus tests for rulers contradict equal rights and the condemnation of forcing religion on others.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Gender identity law is not addressed.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The doctrine claims neutral human ground between groups, but does not discuss left and right.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Dogma 10 says no one can be commended or condemned for their inherited religion, and religions are meant to meet on common ground.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Dogma 3 and 7 ground the state in the equal rights of its inhabitants, not in divine mandate.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; neutrality in public institutions (Dogma 6) is balanced by freedom of faith.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Not addressed; the aim of abolishing war causes is not a call to disband forces.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Not stated; Hillelists are told to stay out of battles between groups, which by analogy suggests neutrality, inferred.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Dogma 2 judges people by personal value, not origin, inferred opposition to hereditary succession.

property-franchise.rationale: Dogma 3 gives all inhabitants equal rights, which excludes wealth-based voting limits.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Equal and absolute justice independent of time and strength (Dogma 7) fits rule by standing laws, inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: Dogma 3 states a country belongs to all inhabitants with equal rights whatever their language or religion, and Dogma 2 rejects ranking by race.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Dogma 2 and 10 condemn persecution for religion and aim at merging across religions.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Dogma 2 names persecution for birth into another race, language or religion as barbarism.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Dogma 10 says religious elements besides conscience and the golden rule are customs that should gradually yield to common human-neutral ones.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Military personnel policy is not addressed.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Dogma 10 keeps God and conscience and forbids imposing views on others, so state atheism is opposed.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Not addressed; a state of equal justice is assumed, inferred.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Dogma 7 requires equal rights for all communities and warns against majority domination.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The sources do not compare charity and welfare, though the ethic is charitable.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Equal rights for all inhabitants (Dogma 3) suggests support, inferred.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; Zamenhof famously left Esperanto free of copyright, but that is not a political doctrine.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Nationalist drilled youth movements conflict with the rejection of ethnic national goals (Dogma 1, 6).

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed; justice for persecuted groups suggests support, inferred.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Pacifist absolutism is not stated; Dogma 7 condemns violence between groups but not individual defence.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Dogma 9 denies national languages in any real sense, and Dogma 1 treats ethnic national aims as group egoism.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Sex and gender theory is not addressed.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Glorifying death for the nation contradicts Dogma 1 and 6 and the aim to end war.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine seeks reconciliation, not struggle between good and evil groups, inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Zamenhof left Zionism, which sought a homeland, and favoured equal rights in each country of residence.

culture-before-state.rationale: Cultural nationalism is a question Hillelism does not take up, as it rejects ethnic aims.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; God is understood by each person's own wisdom and heart (Dogma 10).

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Dogma 3 and 7 give equal rights to all groups, and persecuting a group for birth is barbarism.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Dogma 5 rejects drawing territory on ethnic lines.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Definitions of socialism are not addressed.

person-over-state.rationale: The Essence stresses that each person keeps their homeland, language and religion on a neutral human basis, with equal justice for individuals.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Homaranismo is described as a moral and religious philosophy for uniting people, grounded in God as the highest power.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Dogma 1 calls group egoism along ethnic lines something to disappear, and Dogma 2 says persecuting someone for race is barbarism.

racial-pride.rationale: Dogma 8 says ethnic group is one's race and groups should avoid chauvinism, pride in group is not a value; Dogma 1 opposes group egoism.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Equal rights are meant to abolish the causes of all wars (Dogma 7), consistent with limiting force to defence, though not stated as doctrine.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Dogma 9 says Hillelists deny national languages exist in any real sense and Dogma 8 replaces nation with citizens of one fatherland.

communal-electorates.rationale: Dogma 3 gives all inhabitants equal rights as citizens and Dogma 6 wants neutral public institutions, which weighs against separate religious electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Not addressed; opposition to hostile group conspiracies suggests disagreement, inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: Dogma 7 aims at abolishing causes of wars and Zamenhof sought a world without war (Wikipedia), implying reduction of arms.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Secret diplomacy is not addressed, though the doctrine seeks peace.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Monopoly on force is not discussed.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Global economic order is not addressed.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The doctrine works for equal rights within the existing state and not for its destruction (Dogma 3, 7).

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Voluntaryist economic ideas are not addressed.

sacred-nation.rationale: Dogma 1 calls ethnic national aims group egoism and human hatred, and Zamenhof wrote in 1914 that all nationalism brings great unhappiness.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Regional exploitation theory is not addressed.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The Essence and Dogma 2 rest on common humanity beyond group origin, though human nature is not discussed in these terms.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Homaranismo is framed as a bridge between religions with shared moral principles, though not a claim that all religions teach one doctrine.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed; golden-rule ethics suggest agreement with a ban, inferred.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; equal justice for all suggests agreement, inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed; Dogma 9 says one's language is the one one knows, a related but different point.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Environmental liability law is not addressed.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Dogma 4 forbids forcing language on others, and Dogma 6 asks neutral languages in public institutions, so compulsion is unlikely.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Union membership rules are not addressed.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Dogma 7 calls for equal rights for all religions, and Dogma 10 says no one can be commended or condemned for a traditional religion.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Definitions of democracy are not addressed.

premarital-sex.rationale: Sexual morality is not addressed; Dogma 10 leaves custom aside except the golden rule.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Not addressed; equal justice independent of strength suggests disagreement, inferred.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Dogma 8 and 9 avoid nation-centred language, and Dogma 6 wants neutral public institutions, so nation-centred history teaching is unlikely; inferred.

missingStatements.text: A neutral shared language should be used between peoples of different languages in order to reduce hatred between them.
missingStatements.rationale: Dogma 9 and Dogma 4 name a neutral language, currently Esperanto, as the basis for dealing across ethnic lines, and Zamenhof saw misunderstanding as a cause of hatred.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to constructed-language movements; few other ideologies take a side, so it would not earn a place in the bank.

missingStatements.text: Public institutions should use a language and festivals that are neutral among the state's ethnic and religious groups, while each group runs its own schools.
missingStatements.rationale: Dogma 6 sets out exactly this arrangement of neutral public institutions with separate group schools.

notes: Statements on economics and most institutional questions are not addressed by Zamenhof; they are low-confidence inferences or zero. Only the questions on nationalism, ethnic equality, religion, war and language have documented positions.
